reviews.t: I'd recommend googling some info about them before buying
reviews.x: If you've never used a boar bristle brush before (or any natural type of natural bristle, I suspect), I'd recommend googling some info about them before buying. You don't use them quite the same way you'd use a brush with hard plastic bristles. You definitely want to comb the tangles out of your hair first, for example, and wait until your hair is dry to brush it. (Maybe you're supposed to do those things anyway, for all I know -- I have shorter hair so it's easier for me to use brushes incorrec

This is NOT all boar bristle, it is about 50% nylon bristles. The inner bristles of each little cluster are nylon, and the outer are boar (or at least some kind of animal). I have included pictures.  It is INCREDIBLY static-causing. I am returning it immediately.
Product came in a damaged box and looked as if it was either used or had terrible quality. Also there are slightly more nylon pieces than boar bristles. Returning.  Not going to rebuy.

reviews.t: hardly any boars hair. do not buy!
reviews.x: false advertising!!!! the bristles are mostly nylon not boars hair. they are also very short so it will not penetrate hair very well unless you have a crew cut. the bristles are not attached well and fall out while i attempt to use it,  the company offers free returns but customers have to pay shipping. buy a more expensive real boars hair brush this one is not a bargain! amazon should check into the deceptive description.

reviews.t: I did not like it. It had a bad smell
reviews.x: I did not like it. It had a bad smell, bristles are very thick and hard, and some are falling out

Literally.  The first time is got slightly damp, it developed a smell, which transfers to your hair when you use it.  Several washings were not enough to remove the smell from the brush.  I have been much happier with the $5 Conair Boars Hair Brush that I picked up from my local store (and unlike this bru

First thing I noticed was a very powerful chemical smell upon opening the box,followed by seeing that  the majority of bristles were a  uniform length/width nylon... VERY disappointing. I feel cheated both by the seller and the reviewers who did not bring this obvious deception to light.

reviews.t: This is such a crappy brush. I am 17 years old
reviews.x: This is such a crappy brush. I am 17 years old, and I have long, thick hair. I want to grow my hair out incredibly long so I can cut and donate it. If I want to do so, I must have healthy hair. Boar bristle brushes are extremely good for hair, so I bought one. This one sucks. This is NOT for all hair types. The bristles are so short, making it impossible to efficiently brush thick hair. If you are looking into this brush, do not purchase it unless you have fine hair.

reviews.t: This brush is not for women. The bristles are ...
reviews.x: This brush is not for women.  The bristles are 1/2 inch long and only appropriate for short, short hair.  I wish the description had mentioned this detail.

You get what you pay for when buying a boar bristle brush.  This brush has a great feel to it, the handle and weight of the brush in my hand  work well to guide the brush through my long hair.  The purpose of a BBB is not to detangle; it is to stimulate the scalp, spread sebum throughout your length, and use as a finishing brush. One should use a detangle brush or comb before brushing with a BBB. I use the GranNatuarals Boar Bristle Brush in the morning and at night, and I never use it on wash d

It's a hairbrush that's made out of hair. Holy moly! Want to know what it's like to brush your hair with hair? Well buddy boy have I got a brush for you, it's this one! Its hair that the fine people at GranNaturals cleverly affixed to a piece of wood. But they didn't stop there, they then took that piece of hairy wood and carved a handle at the bottom. And talk about ergonomics, that sucker feels almost as good in your bald hand as it does on your hairy head! This isn't your grandpa's hairbrush,

This made my hair so so smooth. Unfortunately, it also make it very greasy. I looked like a dude for a 50’s movie. Not a cute look.  I made it greasy and frizzy at the same time. I had to wash my hair more often then not just to make it look normal.  I also feel like this was damaging my hair. I just don’t think this was right for my hair type. Let’s just say I no long use this.  On the plus side, the you get what you pay for. The quality is there and it is exactly what you think it is.

This product is a very poor choice for keeping brats in line.  After only two solid minutes of swatting my 21 year old boy's behind, this product split right in two.  Made it even worse when he started laughing.  Look elsewhere for your discipline needs.

reviews.t: A Worthy Brush for a Gentleman
reviews.x: A nice large brush.  No loose bristles.  The wood has a pleasing grain.  The quality of this brush exceeds the price.  Can readily double as a spanking paddle in a pinch.
I really like this brush, it is a great size and seems to work even better than my other boar hair brush. The handle is nice quality as well.

reviews.t: Using a boar bristle brush requires a little research and practice to get it right.
reviews.x: I've never used a boar bristle brush before. At first I was slightly dismayed at how short the bristles are. I didn't think they would get through my thickish wavy hair...and I was right. But I did a little research and found that they aren't supposed to. This type of brush is not intended for detangling. For that I use a very wide-toothed comb. What this brush is for is to distribute oils from the scalp down the length of the hair. This it does extremely well. The best way do accomplish this wi
I live in an arid mountain environment and this brush has immediately smoothed my hair and already made more shiny! Love it~

The first thing I noticed when I bought the brush was that it had a terrible smell. I hoped the smell would dissipate but it's been over a week and it still reeks. To make matters worse, the smell transfers to my hair. With regard to how it brushes, I have to say I'm disappointed. The bristles only reach the very top layer of hair. I have very thick, waist-length hair and this brush just isn't working for me. I didn't notice that it distributed that natural oils in my hair at all. I've had bette

reviews.t: She had amazing hair her whole life
reviews.x: Recently, I remembered that my grandmother always swore by natural boar bristle brushes. She had amazing hair her whole life. This brush is of excellent quality. The bristles are not too hard and not too soft. I noticed an immediate improvement in the shine of my hair and my scalp feels really great after brushing. I'm hoping this will also help with my thinning hair issues. I will report back if I see an improvement over time. Meanwhile, I am very pleased with this brush regardless as to whethe

reviews.t: It does it's job, but could have been designed better
reviews.x: On the positive side, the brush does help to make my (short) hair more manageable, presumably by distributing hair oils more evenly. But I was disappointed at the clunky appearance of the brush. I have fairly small hands, and the brush seems too wide and over-sized. Of course a wooden handle is durable, that goes without saying. reviews.t: Very useful for just daily brushing!
reviews.x: I have been using these brushes for about 3 years and honestly they’re the cheapest but best for just daily brushing for my hair when I don’t want to detangle every day. Eventually the bristles will fall out and I usually use that as an indicator that it is time to replace my brush. I’ve had one last as little as 6 months and another one last the whole year. My hair before using these was up to my shoulders 3 years ago so it definitely has helped me keep my length with other parts of my hair reg

I actually love the design of the brush, but this brush is not for thick hair! I love the way it makes my hair feel, but it doesn't get all the way through my hair. I'm going to keep searching until I find a Boar a Bristle brush for thick hair!

claims.text: Many reviewers report the brush is not 100% boar bristle, with a large share of nylon/plastic bristles instead.
Several reviewers complain of a chemical or unpleasant smell, sometimes transferring to hair when damp.
Multiple reviewers report bristles falling out, including right out of the box or during use.
Some reviewers say the short bristles don't penetrate thick or long hair well.
A few positive reviewers praise the brush's feel, weight, and scalp-stimulating performance for long hair.

qa.q: Will this brush work for fine, thin hair without making it static?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: Are the boar bristles soft enough for sensitive scalps?
qa.answer: Reviews disagree on softness: one reviewer says the bristles are "not too hard and not too soft" and their scalp feels great after brushing [3], but no review directly addresses sensitive scalps specifically.

claims.text: The bristles are not too hard and not too soft, and the scalp feels great after brushing.

qa.q: How well does it detangle long hair without pulling?
qa.answer: Not enough evidence in reviews to answer this.

qa.q: Does the wooden handle feel sturdy and well-made?
qa.answer: Reviews describe the handle positively: one calls it "nice quality" [5], another praises its ergonomics [4], and another notes a wooden handle is durable [1]. However, one reviewer reported the product looked used or of terrible quality [6].

claims.text: One reviewer felt the product looked used or had terrible quality.

qa.q: Is the brush easy to clean and does it have any smell?
qa.answer: Reviews report a bad smell that transfers to hair and persists despite washing [1][2][3], though some reviewers mention no smell [4][5]. On cleaning, one reviewer says several washings were not enough to remove the smell [3], so reviews do not support that it is easy to clean.

claims.text: The brush had a bad smell that transfers to hair and persists over a week [1][2][3].
Several washings were not enough to remove the smell from the brush [3].
Some reviewers did not mention any smell [4][5].
